verification_candidates.claim_text: Mendelian-randomization studies show that increasing alcohol consumption raises the risk of hypertension, dementia, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and all-cause mortality.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: any standard deviation and increase in the consumption of alcohol leads to a greater increase in the risk of everything from hypertension to dementia to cardiovascular disease to cancer to all-cause mortality
verification_candidates.rationale: Specific dose-response mortality/disease risk claim from genetic epidemiology studies is checkable.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Alcohol has no dose that is health-helpful, and its harm increases at higher doses.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Under low doses, probably not terribly bad, but under escalating doses, it's actually quite negative.
verification_candidates.rationale: Dose-response safety claim about alcohol's health effects is checkable.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Drinking alcohol too close to bedtime disrupts sleep.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: I think most people will observe that if you drink a little bit too close to bed, your sleep is going to be disrupted.
verification_candidates.rationale: Claim linking alcohol timing to sleep disruption is checkable against sleep research.
